output.brief: The wrong expiry dates did not come from the agency operators or the printer firmware. Printer job records show that, from 4 Oct, the line integration service sent a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol, and the printers printed it as received with no operator overrides. Before that, every job was correct, including the jobs run on the new firmware and by the new operators. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month value in the ERP that is only valid from March 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. The integration service appears to have picked up the future-dated value anyway, which contradicts the vendor's claim. The failure also affected 2 lots from Line 1 day shift, so it isn't only Line 3 nights. The camera passed these cartons because it only checks print against the job data. I am fairly confident of this. Two other products carry future-dated edits and may be affected, but that is unconfirmed. Next steps: do not issue the warnings or remove the operators. Fix the Veltranol ERP record. Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the warehouse lots. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record. Check the two other products with future-dated edits. Ask the vendor to explain why the future-dated value was read. Hold off on a 12-month reconciliation and on over-labelling.
